skill.name: inkos

content.value_statement: Creative teams need a reliable way to develop long-form stories while preserving intent, facts, revisions, and production context. InkOS organizes planning, writing, review, revision, and export through typed actions and persisted artifacts.
actual_capabilities: Plans novels, short fiction, scripts, storyboards, and interactive films.
Supports derivative projects with explicit lineage and source canon.
Maintains entities, relationships, time, evidence, inventory, and scenes for play-world work.
Provides spot fixes, polishing, rewrites, and structural rework.
Supports multilingual long-document translation with terminology and resumable artifacts.
Supports typed image-prompt assets and image generation for storyboards.
limitations: Requires the InkOS host, Pi agent, and relevant capabilities for execution.
This skill describes workflows; it does not grant write permission or storage access.
CLI examples require a local InkOS installation and user confirmation.
Creative quality depends on source context, model output, and review.

use_cases.title: Develop a long-form novel
use_cases.description: Build a foundation, plan chapters, draft scenes, review evidence, and preserve revisions across a manuscript.

use_cases.title: Produce scripts and storyboards
use_cases.description: Create screenplays, audio dramas, interactive scripts, storyboards, and typed image-prompt assets.

use_cases.title: Manage interactive or derivative fiction
use_cases.description: Design persistent worlds, branching stories, source lineage, canon constraints, and resumable translations.

prompt_templates.title: Start a story foundation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a foundation for a character-driven mystery novel in English, including audience, premise, themes, and constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the next chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the next three chapters from the current manuscript, preserving established facts and identifying unresolved story questions.

prompt_templates.title: Review and revise a passage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review chapter eight against the current reader promise, then propose a targeted rewrite that preserves the artifact authority.

prompt_templates.title: Build an interactive film
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an interactive film with a story tree, persistent flags, branching scenes, storyboard assets, and an exportable playable graph.

output_examples.input: Create a three-chapter mystery outline with a hidden family secret.
output_examples.output: A chapter outline with escalating clues, a midpoint revelation, a final confrontation, and continuity notes for the next draft.

output_examples.input: Review chapter eight against the current reader promise.
output_examples.output: Evidence-backed observations identifying where tension, character motivation, and promised clues are sustained or weakened.

output_examples.input: Translate a long manuscript into French with consistent terminology.
output_examples.output: A resumable translation plan with a terminology list, translated sections, and notes for unresolved source ambiguities.

best_practices: State the audience, genre, language, and desired artifact before creation.
Review persisted artifacts and revisions before requesting structural changes.
Use explicit lineage and source canon for derivative projects.
anti_patterns: Do not treat assistant prose as proof that an artifact was persisted.
Do not request rewrites when review observations are sufficient.
Do not guess storage paths or claim changes without an artifact reference.

faq.question: What is InkOS designed for?
faq.answer: InkOS supports structured creation for stories, scripts, interactive films, open worlds, derivative works, and long-document translation.

faq.question: Does InkOS write files directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that capability actions and host tools control creation and mutation permissions.

faq.question: Can InkOS preserve revisions?
faq.answer: Yes. Its workflow treats artifact revisions as evidence and preserves prior revisions during explicit changes.

faq.question: Can I use InkOS for derivative fiction?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports fan fiction, spinoffs, imitation, and continuation with explicit lineage and source canon.

faq.question: Does InkOS support interactive narratives?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports story trees, flags, persistent entities, scenes, assets, playable graphs, and exports.

faq.question: What does InkOS require?
faq.answer: You need the InkOS host, a Pi agent, relevant capabilities, and a local installation for documented CLI actions.
